notes: Every element/attribute below is sourced from a real, cited docs.mulesoft.com page. Fields that could not be confirmed against a real page were left out rather than guessed -- see 'source' on each entry. This file is data only: it is read by ark/validation/mulesoft_http_connector.py, never hardcoded into generator/mutation/renderer logic, so it stays inspectable and swappable for another connector's schema later.

http:listener-config.description: Global (server-side) element organizing an HTTP Listener's connection settings. Distinct from http:request-config -- a listener-config can never be referenced by an http:request.

http:listener-connection.description: Child of http:listener-config carrying the actual host/port/protocol and, optionally, TLS/reconnection settings.

http:listener.description: Flow-level source (operation) that listens for inbound requests, referencing a listener-config by name via config-ref.

http:request-config.description: Global (client-side) element organizing an HTTP Request operation's connection settings. Distinct from http:listener-config -- a request-config can never be referenced by an http:listener.

http:request-connection.description: Child of http:request-config carrying the actual host/port/protocol and, optionally, TLS/authentication/reconnection settings.

http:request.description: Flow-level operation that makes an outbound HTTP call, referencing a request-config by name via config-ref.

http:authentication.description: Wraps exactly one of the five real, documented authentication schemes for the Request operation. Do not invent a scheme not in required_children_choice below.

http:basic-authentication.description: Username/password sent as an Authorization header.

http:digest-authentication.description: Digest auth: username/password only (no domain/workstation -- that's NTLM, not Digest).

http:ntlm-authentication.description: NTLM auth: username/password required; domain/workstation optional.

oauth:authorization-code-grant-type.description: OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code grant. HTTP Connector documents only OAuth 2.0 -- there is no plain 'OAuth'/OAuth1 scheme.

oauth:client-credentials-grant-type.description: OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials grant -- no callback/authorization URLs needed (no resource-owner redirect step).

reconnect.description: Standard Mule SDK reconnection strategy (not HTTP-specific) -- a fixed number of attempts.

reconnect-forever.description: Standard Mule SDK reconnection strategy (not HTTP-specific) -- retries indefinitely at a fixed frequency.

excluded_by_design.tls:context / tls:key-store / tls:trust-: Real and documented (seen inline in http-connector-xml-reference examples), but deliberately left out of THIS schema file's validated element set -- TLS context is a generic Mule-runtime element shared by every connector, not HTTP-specific, and modeling it precisely (keystore/truststore/protocol enums) is its own reviewable unit. Referenced here only as an allowed, unvalidated optional_children entry so its mere presence doesn't trigger an 'unknown element' failure.
excluded_by_design.http:load-static-resource / http:basic-s: Real, documented HTTP Connector operations, but out of scope for this pass -- Ark's estates only ever need a listener source + request/transform operations (see ark/core/models.py's Step union), so these were never going to be exercised and are excluded rather than speculatively schema'd.
excluded_by_design.OAuth1 / a generic 'OAuth' scheme: Does not exist in the real docs -- HTTP Connector documents OAuth 2.0 only, with two grant types (Authorization Code, Client Credentials). An earlier draft of this task assumed 'Basic / OAuth / OAuth2' as three schemes; the real, verified list is five (Basic, Digest, NTLM, and the two OAuth2 grant types) -- corrected here rather than silently kept.
